reply:
The right leg is built as a true mirror of the left and saved to `s3_legs.polykrom`. To keep the legs from colliding I had to cut the inward hip roll on both legs to −0.5°. The feet are only 8 mm apart, so a wider stance is the real fix.

## What I did
- **Printed parts (PLA, lime / black, TPU pad):** I copied HipRollBracket, HipPitchBracket, Thigh, Shin, AnkleRollBracket, three claws and the sole pad as new `_R` components and mirrored their geometry across Y = 0.
- **Servos:** I inserted five new STS3215 servos from the library, each turned so it matches the mirror image of its left twin. The roll servos are translated; the pitch servos are turned 180° about their long axis; the ankle roll servo is turned 180° about X.
- **Screws:** 20 new M2 library screws sit at the mirrored holes, each rigidly seated on its link.
- **Joints:** each servo case is rigid on its link, each horn is rigid on the link it drives, and each revolute turns about the servo output.
  - The yaw and roll axes point the opposite way to the mirror of the left axes, and the pitch axes keep their direction. That way the same values give mirror-image poses.
  - The torso's existing horn joint `HipYaw_R` (±45°) is now `R_hip_yaw` with the left leg's ±25° limits.

## Verified
- **Mirror:** with all 12 joints driven to the same non-zero values (10/8/30/−50/20/12°), every right link and servo landed at the exact mirror of its left twin, to within 1e-8 mm (the foot to 0.0003 mm).
- **Joint isolation:** a 12-step study moving one joint at a time (kept in the design as `iso_test`) showed each joint moves only its own leg's parts below it. The torso and the other leg never moved.
- **Everything held:** no joint conflicts and no floating chains. Every right-leg part is in a 1–6 revolute chain back to the torso. Nothing is grounded, and the lowest point is at z = 0.
- **Overlap at zero (`inspect.interference`):** the mesh check found only screw-thread engagement and the claw-in-socket contacts. The exact check of the feet, claws and sole pads found no overlapping volume. The claw contacts couldn't be fully confirmed at the 0.011 mm facet level; the left leg, which I didn't change, gives the same result.
- **Hip roll sweep:** with both legs at the old −25°, the sole pads touch at −0.78°. At the new limits the whole range is clear, both legs together and one leg alone. The **closest gap is 2.879 mm**, between the sole pads, with both legs at −0.5°.
- **Mass and centre of mass:** total mass **1181.3 g**; centre of mass **(8.41, −0.37, 217.52) mm**. The small −Y offset comes from the torso contents.

## Problems and workarounds
- **The left foot couldn't be copied** ("copy geometry differs"). My first mirror stayed linked to the left foot and drifted when the joints moved. I replaced it with an independent copy: I exported the mirrored foot to STEP at zero (`work/foot_r_mirror.step`, which you can delete), re-imported it as `Foot_R` and re-joined it. It now mirrors correctly in every pose, mass 34.86 g like the left.
- **Lateral sway is limited:** the −0.5° inward limit means swaying sideways (one leg out, the other in) can now only go 0.5°. Widening the stance would free that up.
- **Hip yaw also collides:** I checked this but didn't change it, because you asked for the same limits on both legs. Toeing one foot in by **13.48°** hits the other foot, but the yaw limit is ±25°. It needs either a narrower yaw limit or a wider stance.
